crisis.label: High
crisis.detail: Sep 5-6: The US and Iran fought a direct tanker war - CENTCOM struck three Iranian oil tankers (near Kharg Island, near Jask, and an unladen vessel in the Gulf of Oman after crew evacuation) while Iran fired ballistic missiles at a US carrier and destroyer (both evaded, no US casualties) and hit three oil tankers plus three US-linked vessels in the Strait (Al Jazeera). CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper warned 'if you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost - taking out three of yours.' Sep 7: Mohsen Rezaei, head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said Tehran plans to declare a maritime 'exclusion zone' running from the US naval blockade line into the Strait and the Persian Gulf, with details to follow in 'coming days and weeks' (CBS News). Separately, Iran-Oman talks on a Hormuz traffic-management framework reportedly reached a 'final stage,' with an understanding expected to register with the IMO within days (CBS News) - an unsigned, unregistered step Rezaei's threat directly undercuts. Kpler data show Hormuz transits still depressed, ranging ~5-11 vessels/day this week against a 10-day average of ~13 (Al Jazeera). Separately, two Filipino seafarers were killed Aug 31 when Iran struck the Bahri-operated Saudi tanker Sidr; Oman's navy rescued 16 of 25 crew (Al Jazeera, The National). QatarEnergy force majeure remains extended into early November. Brent rose to $97.10 (-0.07% intraday) and WTI to $92.44 (-0.10%) on Sep 8 (Trading Economics), a six-week high; TTF eased to 71.95 EUR/MWh (+0.2%, Yahoo Finance, Sep 7); the JKM CFD reference is carried at $24.03 (Trading Economics, Sep 4) pending a fresher print. Crisis level holds at 4 (High) - direct strikes continue but Hormuz remains open to reduced traffic; probabilities shift to base 10%, stress 40%, tail 50% to reflect both the Oman framework's progress and the tanker-war/exclusion-zone escalation.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: Iran and Oman's traffic-management framework, reported at a 'final stage' with IMO registration expected within days, is signed and monitored; a restored, verified reopening lowers Brent toward $75-85, while Qatar's force majeure keeps LNG availability constrained into early November.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: The Oman framework registers but traffic stays selective under Iranian fees, sanctions pressure and the threatened exclusion zone; Brent holds $85-105 and JKM stays elevated while Qatar's force majeure runs into early November.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: Iran declares and enforces its threatened Hormuz exclusion zone, the Oman framework collapses, or the tanker war widens into a broader multi-front exchange; Brent returns to $105-135+/bbl and JKM moves above $30/MMBtu.
